figures.caption: Start with verifiable documentation. License, insurance, references, scope, and responsible contacts should support the actual work being proposed.

figures.alt: Commercial planning table with abstract drawings, estimating tools, blank clipboard, and coordination materials
figures.caption: The right contractor can explain who will manage the project, how scope becomes a fixed price, what assumptions remain, and how decisions will be documented before work begins.
figures.before: 2. Who Will Actually Be Running My Project?

figures.caption: A written scope and permit plan should connect the field sequence to inspections and responsibilities. That makes it easier to understand what is included before a contract is signed.
figures.before: 4. Can You Provide a Written Scope and Fixed Price Before I Sign?
